title: Causal Evidence for a Neural Component of Spatially Global Hemodynamic Signals.
abstract: In this issue of Neuron, Turchi et al. (2018) reversibly inactivate the basal forebrain to show that this region magnifies global neocortical signal fluctuations without altering the topography of canonical resting-state networks. Thus, spatially diffuse signals measurable via functional neuroimaging may track large-scale neuromodulatory state changes in the primate brain.
